senses.definition: A thin, flat, circular plate or similar object.
examples: A coin is a disc of metal.
Venus's disc cut off light from the Sun.

quotes.text: [A] peculiar luminous and sinuous marking appeared on the unillumined half of the inner planet, and almost simultaneously a faint dark mark of a similar sinuous character was detected upon a photograph of the Martian disc.
quotes.reference: 1898, H.G. Wells, The War of the Worlds, London: William Heinemann, page 300:

senses.definition: A vinyl phonograph or gramophone record.
examples: Turn the disc over, after it has finished.

senses.definition: (botany) The flat surface of an organ, as a leaf, any flat, round growth.
(disc sports) Ellipsis of flying disc; synonym of frisbee; generic name for the trademark Frisbee.
(agriculture) To harrow with a disc harrow.

quotes.text: It is held that discing is as much value to lucerne as cultivation is to corn.
quotes.reference: 1901 October 11, “Discing Lucerne”, in The Agricultural Journal and Mining Record, volume 4, number 16, page 488:

senses.definition: (aviation, of a propeller) To move towards, or operate at, zero blade pitch, orienting the propeller blades face-on to the oncoming airflow and maximizing the drag generated by the propeller.
examples: In the air, the asymmetric drag generated by a discing propeller can result in loss of control of the airplane.
